summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Jan 2.5/1181)

data.turoyo: Abre d Alyaske aṯi qamayto, qṭəlle hawo. Aṯi u ʕIsa d bə Kečo kəmminale, hawo ste mḥəlalle, črəfle harke, hawo hawi kule admo, əmmi, qṭəlle hawo ste.
data.translation: Alyaske's son came first; he killed that one. Isa of the Kecho family came, as we call him; they shot him too. It grazed him here; he became all blood, they say, and they killed that one too.

rationale: First Preterit cell and sole new injury-sense example; full shooting-to-blood context supplies the semantic evidence. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New sense 2: (durch einen Schuss) verletzen (genaue Art ungesichert)
rationale: črəfle harke occurs between shooting and the victim becoming all blood. One attestation supports injury, but graze/chip/superficial in the reader proposal is narrower than the independently available Turoyo evidence.

94/260 reads 'bi gorəsto', with s, not š. The supplied glossary also has 'gorəsto' and plural 'gorəsyoṯe' in the handmill examples under grs1, ytw and fyd. This changes a consonant rather than a clitic boundary or vowel diacritic.

summary: Die Reihenfolge kosaymənne qatakiri ... kočərfənne bi gorəsto trennt vorherige Reinigung und Brechen in der Handmühle. Das Herauswerfen von Steinchen ist nicht die Bedeutung von črf.
Generische Mehrzahl der Tätigen, suffigierter betroffener Gegenstand -nne und b- für die Handmühle passen genau zur bestehenden Glosse. Der Instrumentenrahmen ist schon im Glossar zitiert.
Die leichte Schreibungsabweichung gorəsto gegenüber gorəšto wird nicht normalisiert und erzeugt keinen neuen Beleg.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; English quotations are retained verbatim and are not edition translations.
The inherited grain-breaking meaning and its handmill example remain unchanged. Jan supplies a Preterit form in a shooting report, a new domain with a bodily patient rather than food.

The machine translation graze is retained only as a quoted aid. harke is deictic, the patient is understood, and a bullet is not overtly named as subject; exact injury and valency cannot be recovered.
A single attestation is enough to propose the broad injury sense, explicitly provisional in its precise action; it does not justify chip, superficial wound or a technical ballistic meaning.
Confirm the root and exact action of črəfle harke in Jan 2.5/1181: graze, cut, crush or otherwise injure? Identify the l-suffix role, implicit subject and indicated body site.
